title: "patrinia yellow" for Clarinet and Computer
summary: An eleven-minute composition and live performance for clarinet and computer expressing the annual cycle of the yellow patrinia (ominaeshi) plant. The sound consists of the clarinet, parts of the clarinet recorded in real time, and computer processing of those recordings, in three sections: clarinet and computer together, a computer solo, and clarinet and computer again. It premiered in Korea in 2013 and received an Excellence Award in the Art Division of the 18th Japan Media Arts Festival (2014).

title: #MementoMori
summary: #MementoMori is a 2.35 x 1.45 m light box with a backlit print lit by LEDs, connected to a pre-programmed light-flashing device with 10 reactions. title: (antiquated) Augmented Reality
summary: (antiquated) Augmented Reality is a live performance directed by Christine Marie (producer Nion McEvoy) in which an ensemble of dancers (Taylor Unwin, Sandra Ruiz, Melissa Ferrari) performs as giant stereoscopic shadows, up to about 30 feet tall, cast with a non-digital, pre-cinematic stereo imaging technique. The audience views the shadows through anaglyph 3D glasses, so that the figures appear to step off the screen and reach into the room. It was shown in the Films and Performances part of the Sundance Film Festival's New Frontier programme in 2019.

title: 2.6g 329m/s (Bulletproof Skin)
summary: 2.6g 329m/s, also known as Bulletproof Skin, is a bio-art project in which in vitro human skin was reinforced with spider silk produced by genetically modified organisms (transgenic goats and silkworms) and then shot at with .22 calibre Long Rifle bullets; the title is the bullet weight and velocity a Type 1 bulletproof vest must stop. The skin stopped bullets fired at reduced speed but not at full speed. It was made with the Forensic Genomics Consortium Netherlands, Utah State University, Leiden University Medical Center and the Netherlands Forensic Institute.

title: 3FACE
summary: An edition of 4,096 NFT artworks on the Ethereum blockchain, released through the platform Outland. Each 3FACE reads its owner's wallet and public transaction history, interprets it through a personality model of Nature, Nurture and Posture developed by Cheng, and renders a generative portrait; the owner can update the reading as the wallet accrues more history. MoMA and the Whitney Museum acquired editions in 2023.

title: 3SDC (Sunlight, Soil & Shit (De)Cycle)
artist: Oron Catts, Ionat Zurr & Steve Berrick
summary: A working installation made of four linked parts: a compost-heated incubator growing mouse muscle cells as lab-grown meat, an alkaline hydrolysis unit that turns tissue and slaughterhouse refuse into fertiliser, hydroponic beds growing plants without soil, and a control room collecting sensor data from the other parts. It was first staged as a three-week durational experiment at PS Art Space, Fremantle, in February 2022, with public workshops, a symposium, dinner events, live streaming and a documentary. It received an Award of Distinction in Artificial Intelligence & Life Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2023.

title: [help me know the truth]
summary: [help me know the truth] is a networked software installation in which visitors take a selfie that is sent to tablets around the gallery. Using the reverse-correlation method from cognitive neuroscience, the software adds noise to the face and other visitors choose between two altered versions in response to prompts such as which face is more trustworthy or which is the terrorist. The face resulting from repeated choices is shown on a large projection.

title: A Tale of Two Seeds: Sound and Silence in Latin America's Andean Plain
summary: A sound installation built from field recordings of soils and plants in Colombia's Eastern Plains, recorded above and below ground, together with recordings of the electrical conductivity of soy and amaranth plants, which are sonified. FACT describes the recordings as contrasting soy monocultures with soy-amaranth polycultures, where amaranth grows despite herbicide use. Accompanying video works (On Vegetal Politics, Botánica Transgénica) and a blockchain application address the stock-market valuation and patenting of genetically modified plants; the work received the 2023 Prix Ars Electronica Golden Nica in Digital Musics & Sound Art.

title: A Thousand Thoughts
summary: A Thousand Thoughts is a 'live documentary' portrait of the Kronos Quartet by Sam Green and Joe Bini, who are credited together with directing, writing and editing it. Green narrates live on stage while the Kronos Quartet performs the score, alongside archival footage, photos and interviews with the quartet and collaborators such as Philip Glass, Laurie Anderson, Terry Riley, Tanya Tagaq and Steve Reich. It premiered at the Sundance Film Festival's New Frontier section in 2018 and toured to venues including the Wexner Center and the Barbican Hall, London.

quotes.text: From the beginning, I felt like this form was perfect for a portrait of Kronos. They’ve been around for 40-plus years, have put out dozens of albums, collaborated with everyone from Astor Piazzolla to Laurie Anderson – the scale and scope of their oeuvre is incredible. But the most powerful thing about them really is hearing them play live.
quotes.speaker: Sam Green
quotes.source: Robert Greene, 'A cinema-in-the-moment: Sam Green on A Thousand Thoughts and the ‘live documentary’', Sight and Sound (BFI), 2018

quotes.text: So with these live documentary pieces, it’s super fun and challenging to toggle back and forth between these two modes of experience. At certain points in A Thousand Thoughts the viewer should be completely glued to the screen, but at other points we make you radically aware of being in the room and sharing this moment.
quotes.speaker: Sam Green
quotes.source: Robert Greene, 'A cinema-in-the-moment: Sam Green on A Thousand Thoughts and the ‘live documentary’', Sight and Sound (BFI), 2018

quotes.text: And with this piece in particular I knew that using some silence could be a powerful thing – to get the audience to really engage with their ears. With A Thousand Thoughts I knew I wanted people to listen in a different and much more engaged manner – that that would make the Quartet’s music much more of a profound experience.
quotes.speaker: Sam Green
quotes.source: Robert Greene, 'A cinema-in-the-moment: Sam Green on A Thousand Thoughts and the ‘live documentary’', Sight and Sound (BFI), 2018

quotes.text: For me it was important not to make a tribute film. That was something I wanted to avoid. It’s a portrait of them but it uses a portrait of them to explore bigger ideas, which I think was a good solution.
quotes.speaker: Sam Green
quotes.source: 'Q&A: Sam Green on A Thousand Thoughts', Wexner Center for the Arts blog, 2018

quotes.text: So in the context of this new world, I feel strongly that there is a politics around the form of live cinema that’s important. The idea of us traveling all the way to London, you buying a ticket and all of us turning off our phones, being 100 percent present, and together creating something that will never happen the same way twice – there’s something not only magical about that, but there’s also something politically valuable too. Sitting in a dark room with strangers is a radical act!

quotes.source: Robert Greene, 'A cinema-in-the-moment: Sam Green on A Thousand Thoughts and the ‘live documentary’', Sight and Sound (BFI), 2018

title: Avatar Robot Cafe DAWN ver.β
summary: Avatar Robot Cafe DAWN ver.β is a permanent café in Nihonbashi, Tokyo, run by Ory Lab, where people who have difficulty going out because of illness, disability, caregiving or distance work as “pilots”, remotely operating the avatar robots OriHime and OriHime-D from home or hospital through the robots' cameras, microphones and speakers, in some cases by eye-gaze input. title: Baitul Ma'mur: House of Angels
summary: A bio-art project by Sarah Khan and Joe Davis that encodes the Arabic phrase "Subhan Allah" multiple times into synthesized DNA molecules, using a coding scheme modelled on the repeating geometries of Islamic art; according to the artists, a 1mm layer of this DNA on the head of a straight pin holds 2.417 quintillion repetitions ("angels"). The work is presented with a glass and aluminum "Baitul Ma'mur" structure with electronics, project graphics and a short documentary film. It received an Honorary Mention in the Prix Ars Electronica 2021, Artificial Intelligence & Life Art category.

title: Balance From Within
summary: Balance From Within is a 170-year-old sofa that balances on one of its four legs. A computer-controlled mechanism inside it, based on the reaction wheel used in satellites, keeps correcting its position, and its motors make humming and creaking sounds. A push from a visitor or another outside force can knock it over; its main parts are held together with magnets so that it can be put back together. It received an Award of Distinction for Interactive Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2014.

summary: An installation made in 2020 consisting of a video-essay, two 3D-printed busts and an augmented reality application. summary: Blade Runner—Autoencoded is a film made by training an autoencoder, a type of generative neural network, on every frame of Ridley Scott's Blade Runner (1982) and then having it reconstruct each frame in order. It was made as the artist's MSci dissertation project in Creative Computing at Goldsmiths, University of London.

summary: Broken Spectre (2022) is a feature-length immersive video installation (about 70–74 minutes) on deforestation and environmental crime along the Trans-Amazonian Highway in the Brazilian Amazon, made with cinematographer Trevor Tweeten and composer Ben Frost. title: Carbon Black
summary: Carbon Black (Noir de carbone) is a series of 15 photographic prints of the sky made in collaboration with climate modellers Rita van Dingenen and Jean-Philippe Putaud (Joint Research Centre, European Commission). summary: An installation made for the 36th Bienal de São Paulo (2025): 11 suspended panels of recycled matchbox fragments on thin wooden slats, among which 64 motor-driven rope pendulums carrying pieces of coal strike leather drums. quotes.text: That is what a catastrophe is: everything comes crashing down. quotes.text: The history of humanity is like a great battle of materialities. When I received the invitation from the Bienal, it was a great opportunity to reflect on the materials I’ve been researching and how they might collide with one another, generating friction. The matchboxes that carry fire. Coal, which is essentially a fossilized, burned tree; which fueled industrial production in the past century; which brought us to our current technological model—driven and shaped by the historical rhythms that fire (and water) have created over time. In catástrofe orquestra #1 (Ato I), I am interested in the violent act of the coal pendulums being dropped onto the drum as a representation of this historical thread.

The catastrophe ceases to be an isolated event and comes to be seen as a functioning system, governing our lives at every moment.

title: Chijikinkutsu
summary: A sound installation made of water, sewing needles, glass tumblers and coils of copper wire. Magnetized needles float on the water in the tumblers and align north-south with the earth's magnetic field; when current is switched to a coil on the outside of a tumbler, the temporary magnetic field draws the needle against the glass, producing a faint sound, with the switching sequenced by MIDI from an iPad app through custom controllers. The title combines "chijiki" (geomagnetism) and "suikinkutsu", an Edo-period sound device for Japanese gardens; the work received the Golden Nica for Digital Musics & Sound Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2015.

title: Chuly? Chuly
summary: An XR video game and live motion-capture performance (Ukrainian title Чули? Чули, 'Have you heard? We've heard' / 'Have you felt it? In the first act a player crosses a game world guided by an AI-processed narration of a woman's story of seeing giants; in the second a dancer in an inertial motion-capture suit, whose calibration drifts, enters, and player and dancer exchange suit parts and controller, so the player becomes a non-player character and the dancer controls the camera. According to the gallery, participants enter an ephemeral network through fungible tokens inscribed in code, in a collective performance planned to last a decade; the work was presented in partnership with Shape.

title: Collective Body
summary: Collective Body is a 19-minute multi-user virtual reality dance experience set in a New Mexican storm, in which participants are guided through stages: beginning alone, discovering the unfamiliar, first encounters and moving together. An algorithmic system analyses each participant's movement and assigns one of sixteen avatars, each represented as a natural element with its own musical theme; participants then meet one other person and finally the whole group. It runs on Meta Quest 3 headsets with almost full-body tracking and no other wearables; it was shown at Venice Immersive 2025 and at Lincoln Center.

quotes.text: I was asking myself, “What does this mean for our embodied selves? What does it mean for the way we express ourselves physically if we’re only going to be these avatars? title: Community of Parting
summary: Community of Parting is a 72-minute film presented as a double-channel video installation in the Korean Pavilion of the 58th Venice Biennale (2019). It invokes the Korean shamanic myth of the abandoned princess Bari and combines shamanic ritual performances and chants by shaman Koh Sunahn of Jeju Island, nature and cityscapes, archival material, aerial imagery, poetry, voiceover and soundscapes. It was filmed in locations including Jeju Island, the DMZ, South Korea, North Korea, Kazakhstan, Japan, China, the United States and Germany, with narratives by South Korean, North Korean and diasporic women.

title: Compose
summary: Yuko Mohri's exhibition for the Japan Pavilion at the 60th Venice Biennale (20 April to 24 November 2024), curated by Sook-Kyung Lee, made of two site-specific installations built mostly from materials found locally. In Moré Moré (Leaky), the artist creates water leaks in the pavilion and catches them with household goods, with pumps circulating the water through a large kinetic sculpture; rain can enter through the open ceiling. In Decomposition, electrodes in local fruit turn their changing moisture into signals that modulate drone sounds and lights as the fruit ripens and decays, after which it goes to compost.

title: Convergence
summary: Convergence is a 35-minute piece for string ensemble and AI system, made with Ensemble Resonanz, that exists as a staged version (premiered in Bonn, October 2020; revised in Dresden, 2023) and a digital-only streamed version (premiered February 2021, commissioned by Eclat Festival). Deep-learning models (auto-encoders and GANs, with audio programming by IRCAM researchers) learn features of the musicians' faces, bodies and voices, and the performers, guided by a computer voice, interact with the generated counterparts of themselves. It won the 2021 Prix Ars Electronica Golden Nica for Digital Musics & Sound Art.

title: Conversations Beyond the Ordinary
summary: Conversations Beyond the Ordinary is an ensemble of three interactive installations (a coffee vending machine, a photocopier and a microwave) fitted with sensors, custom software and generative AI so that they converse with visitors. Visitors have to persuade the coffee machine to brew them a coffee, draw doodles that the photocopier turns into rendered prints they can take home, and use the microwave to give a voice to objects placed inside it. It received an Honorary Mention in Interactive Art+ at Prix Ars Electronica 2024 and was shown at the Ars Electronica Festival 2024; the coffee machine and microwave were developed during a residency at iii (instrument inventors initiative).

title: Corpus Nil
summary: Corpus Nil is a 20-25 minute performance for one human performer and artificial-intelligence algorithms. In a dark space, Donnarumma, partly naked and painted black, performs a slow choreography while biosensors (chip microphones for muscle sounds and EMG electrodes) send data to software that learns his movement and chooses on its own how to generate multichannel sound and light, which in turn affects his movement. It premiered on 6 February 2016 at ZKM Karlsruhe and received an Award of Distinction in Digital Musics & Sound Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2017.

title: Crossings
summary: Crossings is a three-channel video installation (6 minutes 20 seconds per Galleria Continua) about sub-Saharan migrants who leave their home countries hoping to reach Europe, and about their passage through Morocco. Told from the migrants' point of view, it combines voice-over testimonies, still portraits and reconstructed video landscapes to recreate the sensations of the journey. It was shown at the 5th Marrakech Biennale in 2014, at the Ecole supérieure des arts visuels (ESAV), with which it was produced.

title: Crystal Sounds of a Synchrotron
summary: A 38-minute surround-sound (5.1) work composed from frequencies generated by the electron storage ring of Diamond Light Source, the UK's synchrotron, mostly the sounds of electron injections into the accelerator, combined with binaural recordings made in its experimental hall, storage ring and beamlines. title: Dancer from the Peninsula
summary: Dancer from the Peninsula is a multi-channel video installation made for the Korean Pavilion of the 58th Venice Biennale (History Has Failed Us, but No Matter, 2019). It traces the dancer Choi Seung-hee (1911–1969) through her fragmented archive, focusing on the period after 1941 and her aim to create a modern East Asian dance, using found footage and images from her archives. The presentation in Venice also included a large sculptural structure and a small garden installed behind the pavilion.

title: Dead Drops
summary: Dead Drops is an anonymous, offline, peer-to-peer file-sharing network in public space: USB flash drives are cemented into walls, buildings and curbs, each installed empty except for a readme.txt file. Bartholl installed the first five in New York in October 2010 during an Eyebeam residency; the project was shown in MoMA's Talk to Me (2011) and has since spread to many countries.

title: Dominus Trémulo

title: Dust Blooms: A Research Narrative in Artistic Ecology
summary: Dust Blooms examines how well urban flowers filter airborne dust, in three parts. Dust was collected from seven wild roadside plant species on heavily trafficked Berlin streets and analysed under light microscopes; an exhibition laboratory with microscopes, slides, protocols and maps lets visitors look at the dust-covered petals themselves, next to a raised bed of the same species and photographs. It also includes seven botanical engravings printed with the collected street dust and shell gold, and dandelion-based sculptural prototypes made from consumer materials, with Arduino dust sensors that measure atmospheric dust levels.

title: GR-AI-N
summary: GR-AI-N is a digital-craft workflow that uses discarded offcuts from the wood industry: pieces are scanned, AI-powered tools extract their grain patterns, texture and imperfections, and robotic assembly and milling build objects (mirrors, a headboard) as 3D mosaics of irregular pieces that keep the grain continuous. It was developed in the VOJEXT S+T+ARTS residency 'Robotics in Arts and Crafts' in Barcelona and was nominated for the 2024 S+T+ARTS Prize.

title: Grisaille
summary: Grisaille is a two-part mixed-reality painting experience by Teek Mach, with composer Joel Douek, performed in the Sundance Film Festival's New Frontier section from 25 January to 2 February 2019. In part one a visitor puts on an Oculus Go headset in a dark hallway and moves through a virtual copy of it, past a hologram of the artist and a series of her hand-painted VR portraits; in part two the artist, present in the room, draws the visitor's silhouette with Tilt Brush on an HTC Vive Pro, projected live onto the wall and joined to the silhouettes of earlier visitors, while Douek layers festival sounds with original music. Mach performed it eleven hours a day for the nine days of the festival.

title: Grosse Fatigue
summary: Grosse Fatigue is a 13-minute colour video with sound in which overlapping computer windows show footage filmed in the collections of the Smithsonian Institution in Washington, D.C., mixed with images found on the internet and scenes filmed in places such as a pet store and a domestic interior. Over the images a spoken-word poem, written with Jacob Bromberg and voiced by Akwetey Orraca-Tetteh, combines scientific history with creation stories from religious, hermetic and oral traditions. It was made during a Smithsonian Artist Research Fellowship and presented at the 55th Venice Biennale, Il Palazzo Enciclopedico, in 2013.

title: Guanaquerx
summary: Guanaquerx is a four-legged robot modelled on the guanaco, partly made from caña colihue bamboo and dressed in Andean textiles. In January 2024, about 30 people with 58 mules and horses took it across the Andes from Argentina to the Chilean border over seven days, re-enacting the 1817 crossing by San Martín's army; mules carried the robot where the ground was too rough for it. The robot records sound and images, emits a synthetic whinny, beats a drum, waves a flag and carries a plaque with 'Pluriversal Laws of Robotics'. The work won the 2025 Prix Ars Electronica Golden Nica and was shown at the Ars Electronica Festival 2025.

title: HANDMADE
summary: HANDMADE is a video diptych of about 11 minutes, originally conceived for two 4K monitors and presented at MoMA from November 2023 in the ground-floor Gund Lobby on a large media wall. One part shows digitally manipulated footage of a gale-force storm on Lake Huron, filmed by Thornton with a handheld camera while lying down; the other shows a physicist at Caltech making a handwoven sensing device for a research project on antimatter. These are interspersed with film recordings of fluid-dynamics studies that Thornton found during her 2019 residency in the Caltech-Huntington Program in Visual Culture.

title: Harvesting Climate Action
summary: Harvesting Climate Action was a six-week installation in Hackney Service Centre, London (autumn 2025), part of Ling Tan's Low Carbon Chinatown project, made with Hackney Council's Climate Team. Its centre was 100 recyclable cardboard stools, each printed on one side with a 'Climate Action' (from individual to borough-wide) and on the other with the carbon footprint of a meal ingredient, alongside data maps, food-making videos, audio stories and living produce. The installation then became a 'Low Carbon Banquet for a Hundred', where 100 members of the public each took a stool, sat with strangers over low carbon East and Southeast Asian dishes, debated and voted on the actions, and took their stool home; the 100 Climate Actions also exist as an online toolkit. It received an Honorary Mention (Digital Humanity) at Prix Ars Electronica 2026.

title: Hero
summary: Hero is a large-scale, multi-sensory 'vérité' virtual-reality installation by iNK Stories (Navid and Vassiliki Khonsari), produced with Starbreeze, set in a Syrian town during and after a barrel-bomb air raid. Participants wear a VR headset and haptic backpack and walk through a built set whose props (a tire, crates, bricks) mirror the virtual space, with smell, heat, vibration and surround sound; the session lasts about seven minutes and is followed by a recovery room. Syrian refugees placed in the U.S. by ICNA Relief were interviewed and photographed for the piece; it premiered in Sundance New Frontier in January 2018 and was shown at Tribeca Immersive in April 2018.

title: Hidirtina / Sisters
summary: Hidirtina / Sisters is a 9'14" animated video based on a myth from Eritrea and northern Ethiopia about seven immortal sisters living in nature and a hunter who kills a deer, is cursed, and is protected by a piece of a tree until he loses it in a river. The story was told to the artist by a volunteer who answered his open call for folklore to a Habesha diaspora community in New York, and the animation also includes the process of its making, such as email exchanges, café meetings and a brief portrait of the storyteller. It was shown in the 21st Contemporary Art Biennial Sesc_Videobrasil, 'Imagined Communities' (São Paulo, 2019–20).

summary: A multi-panel installation made during an AlUla residency in 2022, named after Hinat, a Nabataean woman whose tomb (Tomb 117) is at Hegra. Painted and photo-transferred collages of AlUla landscapes have rectangles cut out, into which videos are projected; the videos, generated with machine learning from footage of three women from AlUla wearing coloured fabrics, show ghostly figures moving across the landscapes. It was shown in 'Art of the Kingdom' at the Saudi Arabian Museum of Contemporary Art.

quotes.text: For me, the machine is never neutral. It is fantasy—glamour, transformation, seduction—but it is also a tool through which violence is enacted. title: I'm Humanity
summary: I'm Humanity is a pop song by Etsuko Yakushimaru released in 2016 as a digital download, on CD and as a genetically modified microorganism: the song's main chord progression was converted through a codon-based cipher into a 276-nucleotide DNA sequence and inserted into the genome of the cyanobacterium Synechococcus elongatus PCC 7942, which copies it with each cell division. The microorganism was exhibited at KENPOKU ART 2016 in Ibaraki and at YCAM in Yamaguchi, where the song was also performed live by her band Soutaiseiriron with a section arranged to resemble mutation. It received the STARTS Prize 2017 Grand Prize for Artistic Exploration.

title: If You Have Starry Skies in Your Eyes
summary: A prosthetic eye designed, made and worn by the artist, who lost the sight of her right eye as a child; it contains a magnetic sensor, an LED and a battery encapsulated in medical-grade acrylic resin, and lights up when a magnet is brought near. The project, presented with a video, follows an earlier starry-sky-patterned prosthetic eye she wears daily, and received an Award of Distinction in Interactive Art + at Prix Ars Electronica 2024.

title: IGÚN
summary: An ongoing series of StyleGAN models trained on images of Benin Bronzes looted from the Benin Kingdom during the 1897 British invasion, now held in museum collections. It generates synthetic prototypes of objects that might have been cast during the 17-year interregnum (1897–1914), when no Oba commissioned work; datasets were extended with ceremonial heads in wood and pottery because there were too few bronze images to train the model. The Lumen Prize presentation shows video of latent-space interpolations; the work won the Lumen Prize Global South Award in 2021.

title: In 36,000 Ways (Site-Specific Installation)
summary: In 36,000 Ways (Site-Specific Installation) is a single-visitor booth in which the visitor is shown a piece of missile shrapnel the artist collected on front lines in Ukraine. The visitor's presence and physiological signals, including heartbeat, are picked up without contact and shape a low-frequency soundscape. The title refers to the roughly 36,000 fragments a fragmentation weapon breaks into; the booth is a variation of an ongoing project, shown in the IDFA DocLab Competition 2025, with a larger walk-through version in development.

title: In a Small Room
summary: A project titled in full 'In a Small Room: The Gap between Advertising and Reality', made as a Royal College of Art (Information Experience Design) degree project, about cramped housing in London and Seoul and the advertising images used to rent it. title: In Cameras Res
summary: In Cameras Res is a three-channel moving-image installation by CAMP, commissioned by De Appel, Amsterdam, for which automated CCTV (pan-tilt-zoom) cameras were programmed to film landscape sequences of the city. Each film was shot from a single camera position on a historical building (the former Royal Dutch Shell headquarters, now A'DAM Tower; the former NHM building, now Stadsarchief Amsterdam; the former Tetterode printing foundry), each with a distinct editing technique, and certain people recur in the frame. It was shown at De Appel from 16 March to 20 April 2019.

title: In Potentia
summary: In Potentia is an installation in which human foreskin cells are reprogrammed with the induced pluripotent stem cell (iPS) technique into stem cells and then into neurons, forming a living neural network kept in a purpose-built sculptural incubator with an automated feeding and waste system. A multi-electrode array records the network's electrical activity and converts it into sound, so visitors listen to the neural culture rather than see it, as the cells are not visible to the naked eye. It was made with Stuart Hodgetts and Mark Lawson and shown at Kibla, Maribor (2012) and at ISEA2013, Powerhouse Museum, Sydney, among other venues.

title: In Search of Vanished Blood
summary: In Search of Vanished Blood is a room-filling video/shadow play commissioned by dOCUMENTA (13) in 2012: six synchronised films are projected through five rotating Mylar cylinders reverse-painted with figures of soldiers, animals, gods and guns, so that moving images and shadows pass over the walls, floor and visitors. A soundscape, voiced and designed by the artist, speaks from the perspective of Cassandra and draws on texts by Faiz Ahmed Faiz, Christa Wolf, Mahasweta Devi, Samuel Beckett and Heiner Müller. The title comes from a 1965 Urdu poem by Faiz; a single-channel video version is in the M+ collection, Hong Kong.

title: In Vitro
summary: In Vitro is a two-channel, Arabic-language, black-and-white science-fiction film (about 28 minutes) by Larissa Sansour, co-directed with Søren Lind, commissioned by the Danish Arts Foundation for the Danish Pavilion at the 58th Venice Biennale (2019), where it was shown with the sculpture Monument for Lost Time under the title Heirloom. Set after an eco-disaster, it takes place in an abandoned nuclear reactor under Bethlehem converted into an orchard, where scientists prepare to replant the soil with heirloom seeds. The film is a dialogue between the dying founder of the bunker, Dunia, and her successor Alia, who was born underground and carries memories implanted in her.

title: Interface I
summary: A kinetic installation in which 192 DC motors in two facing rows pull vertical strings against each other like a tug of war, while a mesh of red elastic bands couples each string to its neighbours. The motors are driven by random impulses from Geiger-Müller tubes that register natural background radiation, so the shape of the mesh keeps shifting without a programmed choreography. Visitors watch the band network move as the opposing forces push it up or down. The work was first shown as Order+Noise (Interface I) at NOME Gallery, Berlin, in 2016.

title: Interlooped
artist: Maria Guta, Robin Mange, Javier Bello Ruiz, FlexFab
summary: Interlooped is a multi-user mixed-reality installation and live performance in which the visitor, wearing a VR headset, is captured in real time as a low-resolution volumetric (voxel) hologram by depth-sensor cameras, using technology by the Geneva company Imverse. The visitor's movements and those of performer Maria Guta are recorded and replayed as time loops, so the virtual room fills with multiple versions of both; in a second part Guta joins live, dressed as in the recordings. It premiered in New Frontier at the Sundance Film Festival in January 2019.

title: Island Waters

title: K-9_topology
summary: K-9_topology is a series of four projects (2014–2017) about the relationship between humans, dogs and wolves: Ecce Canis (a fragrance made from serotonin of the artist and her dog), I Hunt Nature and Culture Hunts Me (a performance made during a residency at JACANA Wildlife Studios in France, on the relationship between wolf, dog and human), Hybrid Family (a three-month seclusion in which the artist induced lactation and lived with her dogs, ending in a public performance with a puppy) and ARTE_mis (a hybrid cell made by fusing the artist's enucleated egg cell with a somatic cell of her dog, shown frozen under a microscope). For the 2017 CyberArts exhibition in Linz the series was shown together as an installation in the form of a dog stacker, a training tool for show dogs.

title: Labor
summary: Labor is a self-regulating installation in which three glass bioreactors, each incubating one species of human skin bacteria (Staphylococcus epidermidis, Corynebacterium xerosis, Propionibacterium avidum), produce the smell of sweating, stressed bodies without any people involved. The scents combine in a central chamber holding a white T-shirt, and a Raspberry Pi-based system of stirrers, sensors, pumps, heaters and valves runs the process; the installation also includes sweat-stain-transfer prints.

title: Le Miroir

title: Lines of Divergence
summary: Lines of Divergence is a 7'35" video documenting a current land occupation near Pucusana, a fishing village on the outskirts of Lima, where chalk lines drawn in the desert divide newly registered land into plots. Her 2018 solo exhibition at Galerie Gisela Capitain, Cologne, was titled Lines of Divergence, and the video was shown at the 21st Bienal Sesc_Videobrasil (2019).

title: Loophole for All
summary: Loophole for All is an online intervention in which the artist exposed over 200,000 companies registered in the Cayman Islands, leaking their names from the government registry, and offered the identities of these anonymous offshore companies for low-cost sale on the website Loophole4All.com, issuing forged Certificates of Incorporation under his own name and signature. He also set up his own company in the City of London and produced a video documentary of interviews with experts on offshore centres. In exhibitions the work is shown as two video channels and digital prints of the certificates and legal documents, with a flowchart of the operation.

title: Mad Horse City

summary: MetaPhase is an XR piano performance by pianist and researcher Giusy Caruso with the Milan company LWT3, presented at Cremona Musica on 23 September 2022. summary: A silent three-channel video installation (48:49 seamless loop) made from three and a half hours of fixed-camera 4K 120fps footage of waves breaking against rocks as the light and tide change. In the island's main administrative building a four-pillared structure based on the Javanese saka guru holds a shrine-like arrangement of objects referring to the island's history, with painted cutouts of eight animals from Bugis divination diagrams; visitors follow nine archetypal symbols (The Guide, The Witness, The Wrathful Deity and others). In the garden, eight wind-driven wooden instruments strike bamboo plates, and visitors can also turn them by hand.

title: Music of the Spheres
summary: Música de las esferas (Music of the Spheres) is an installation shown in the Cuban Pavilion at the 55th Venice Biennale in 2013: a glass sphere suspended from the ceiling containing a motor-driven music box, with a light box. An empty circular musical staff was laid over an image of the solar system and a note assigned wherever a planet fell; the music box plays the resulting 30-second looped composition of nine notes.

title: Máquina Stella
summary: Máquina Stella is an electromechanical sculpture made of aluminium, Teflon, resistive filaments, electricity, a mechanical system and electronic control, built as a dodecahedron with twelve limbs. Along each limb an electromechanical terminal moves lengthwise to energise a metal filament that glows red hot, in a programme that distributes the available energy between the parts. It received the ARCO/BEEP Electronic Art Award at ARCO Madrid in February 2012.

title: Máquinas Salvajes
summary: Máquinas Salvajes (Wild Machines) consists of biodegradable mechanical sculptures with wooden skeletons and biopolymer skins (agar-agar and gelatin) made from materials of Costa Rican ecosystems. Two were left in the Sarapiquí rainforest and in Orotina to decay or be eaten, which was documented on video; in the exhibition (Lentos Museum, Linz, 2023) the videos are shown with a third sculpture that a sensor sprays with water when visitors are present, gradually degrading it. The project received a 2023 CIFO-Ars Electronica Award.

title: Nairobi Berries
summary: A 360-degree virtual reality film for mobile VR that combines live-action footage of Nairobi with animation and a lyrical voice-over by Mukii; its synopsis describes two women and a man who wrangle in forests full of smoke and beneath still waters. It was made with Electric South's New Dimensions grant and won the first Immersive Encounters Grand Prix at Encounters Film Festival in 2017.

It received an Honorary Mention in Hybrid Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2013.

title: Necomimi
summary: Necomimi is a headband with motorised cat ears driven by a brainwave sensor: the ears rise when the wearer is concentrating, lie down when the wearer is relaxed, and rise and move when both happen at once. It was developed by the neurowear project team at Dentsu, first shown as a prototype at an event in Omotesando, Tokyo, and later manufactured and sold by NeuroSky. It received an Honorary Mention in Interactive Art at the Prix Ars Electronica 2013.

title: Night Charades
summary: Night Charades is a silent AI-generated animation commissioned for the LED facade of the M+ museum in Hong Kong, shown nightly from 22 March to 29 June 2025. Animated characters mime around 50 scenes, gestures and poses from 1980s and 1990s Hong Kong cinema, re-enacting roles originally played by actors such as Leslie Cheung, Maggie Cheung and Chow Yun-fat. An algorithm continuously reshuffles the scenes and characters into new combinations, viewed by passers-by across Victoria Harbour.

title: No Bird
summary: A kinetic installation (265 x 265 x 150 cm) on a sand surface with two machines: a bird-like walking machine that leaves bird footprints in the sand, and a trace-erasing machine following behind that scratches out the tracks with a toothbrush, smooths them with a wire rake and flattens the surface with soft bristles. According to designboom, the movement is triggered by a sensor when a viewer comes close and runs for about two minutes while the viewer stays in range. The duo (Yoo Byoung-Joon and Lim Hee-Young, Seoul) received an Honorary Mention in Interactive Art + at Prix Ars Electronica 2026.

title: NoSearchBar
summary: NoSearchBar is a Chrome browser extension that removes the search bar from every website, including search engines such as google.com, and changes the browser's search provider so that searching from the URL address bar is disabled. title: Now he's out in public and everyone can see
summary: Now he's out in public and everyone can see is an 18-channel video installation in which 18 monitors of different sizes hang on cables at varying heights around a darkened room. A 16-minute narrative edits together excerpts from hundreds of YouTube vlogs in which people comment on viral media scandals involving four famous African American men, whose names are removed so that the speakers seem to discuss one unnamed man; voices sometimes speak in unison and sometimes answer or contradict each other. Visitors move around the room to follow speakers who are never all in view at once. It premiered at LACE (Los Angeles Contemporary Exhibitions) in 2012 and was remade as a single-channel film in 2017.

title: Occupy George
summary: Occupy George is a set of rubber stamps that print infographics on US one-dollar bills, showing statistics on wealth and income disparity in America, such as how much wealth the richest 400 Americans hold or the ratio of CEO to worker pay. title: Open Source Estrogen
summary: Open Source Estrogen is a collaborative research project by Mary Maggic, begun with Byron Rich, that combines biohacking and speculative design around the hormone estrogen, aiming to develop do-it-yourself / do-it-with-others protocols for detecting and extracting it. Its protocols include transgenic yeast sensors for estrogenic compounds, DIY column chromatography with cigarette filters, silica gel and methanol to extract hormones from urine, and solid-phase extraction of estrogenic compounds from water; it is carried out through public workshops, kitchen performance and videos such as Housewives Making Drugs. It received an Honorary Mention in Hybrid Art at the Prix Ars Electronica 2017.

summary: An 8K animation conceived as an installation: a looping cycle of about five minutes showing a giant pyramid filled with hundreds of small black-and-white figures in a hierarchical society, passing through day and night, modelled on Renaissance fresco murals. A cinema version was nominated for the 2021 Academy Award for Animated Short Film, and the work received an Award of Distinction in Computer Animation at Prix Ars Electronica 2021.

summary: Protei is an open-hardware, shape-shifting sailing robot: an unmanned sailboat whose whole hull bends to steer it, developed so it can sail against the wind and tow oil-absorbent material to intercept drifting oil spills. title: Scanning
summary: Scanning is a single-channel video (41:56 mins) in which Amy Lee Sanford places, flips and scans, sheet by sheet, some 250 found letters on thin onion-skin paper. The letters were exchanged over five years between her adoptive mother in the United States and her biological father, who remained in Phnom Penh during the 1970–1975 civil war and the Khmer Rouge takeover in 1975. The work is in the Singapore Art Museum collection and was shown in Cinerama: Art and the Moving Image in Southeast Asia (SAM, 2017).

quotes.text: Within the counterbalance of exhaustion, tension and collision, a narrative slowly emerges. In contemporary image production, artists inevitably rely on lots of different software tools. title: SEFT-1 (Sonda de Exploración Ferroviaria Tripulada)

title: SMOG SEASON
summary: SMOG SEASON is an installation of 80 cigarette packs mounted on 5 motor-driven circular bases, using Bangkok PM 2.5 air-pollution data and the cigarette-equivalence figure from Berkeley Earth (one cigarette per 22 micrograms per cubic meter per day). title: Smoke and Mirrors
summary: A 4m30s data animation based on NASA's Blue Marble photograph: a counter shows atmospheric methane in parts per billion from 1970 to the present while the rotating globe fills with pink smoke, and advertising slogans from the oil industry (e.g. "Out to clean the air", "Unsettled Science", "Doomsday is cancelled") appear across the screen at their dates. It is set to the song "Oh My Heart" and was produced with the studio Parliament, using NOAA, NASA and EEA data. It received the Prix Ars Electronica Golden Nica (New Animation Art) in 2024 and has been shown as a video and in exhibitions.

title: Songs for dying
summary: A 30-minute HD film with installation, co-commissioned by the 13th Gwangju Biennale, Kunsthall Trondheim and the Han Nefkens Foundation, narrated by the voice of a sea turtle, that combines footage around the death and funeral of the artist's grandfather with Jeju Island's shamanic rituals commemorating the 1948 uprising and the 2020 pro-democracy protests in Thailand. title: SQUEEEQUE-SPEAKERDOME
summary: A dome-shaped enclosure built from some 60–70 recycled speaker boxes facing inward, large enough for about half a dozen people. Visitors go inside, take one of four microphones hanging from the ceiling and speak or sing; their voices pass through effects (delay, phaser) and come back out of the speaker walls, so that strangers inside end up making sound together. First built for a performance at Centre des arts actuels Skol (Elektra festival, Montreal) in 2009, it toured festivals in Europe and Canada and became the first acquisition of HEK (Haus der Elektronischen Künste) Basel's media art collection; in 2021 the artist retitled it SQUEEEQUE-SPEAKERDOME and stopped using the word "igloo".

title: Subnormal Europe

Its framing text presents it as an EU-commissioned project in which the performers create live replicas of moments from audiovisual media history, with an interview series published in parallel on Instagram. It received an Honorary Mention in Digital Musics & Sound Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2021.

title: Sunshine Monument
summary: A Whitney artport commission of seven animated black-and-white architectures, one for each weekday, that translate the layout of blocks of text and images on whitney.org into an abstract building populated by wandering figures, centred on a round sun icon and interspersed with text generated by the artist using AI. title: System's Void
summary: System's Void is a sound installation that translates danger signals from Hazardous Gas System (HGS) monitoring at four fracking wells in the United States into sound, accompanied by a video projection of chemical codes used to classify chemicals. title: Taala Village
summary: Taala Village ('Village of Rhythms') is a pixel-art video game newly commissioned for Colomboscope 2026 (Rhythm Alliances). Players move through a virtual island where actions are accompanied by sounds of Sri Lankan instruments such as the thalampata, drums and conch shells, and meet a speculative community that worships fire and practises rituals, legends and folklore, with settings drawn from kovils, Buddhist temples and village habitats.

title: Tahrir Cinema (Vox Populi)
summary: Tahrir Cinema was a public screening space in Tahrir Square, Cairo, that Lara Baladi co-founded with the Egyptian media collective Mosireen during the summer 2011 sit-in; she describes it as the first project to emerge from Vox Populi, her ongoing archive of the 2011 Egyptian revolution. Films and video clips of the revolution were projected on a makeshift screen at the entrance of the square to an audience seated on the ground, and people could also bring and exchange raw footage on USB flash drives and DVDs.

title: TALK SHOW
summary: TALK SHOW is a 27-minute color film with sound, the final part of Jordan Strafer's Loophole trilogy, shown in a dark gallery with armchairs at the Whitney Biennial 2026. It unfolds across two periods: the turn of the millennium, shot in color (including a reenactment of John F. Kennedy Jr.'s last radio exchange before his 1999 plane crash), and the afterlife, shot in black and white. Most of the film is a daytime talk show in which a host questions a panel of men who confess to rapes while the women they raped watch from backstage; the screenplay draws on news footage and self-help media.

title: tele-present water
summary: tele-present water is a kinetic installation in which a lattice of wooden rods hangs from nylon threads and is moved by seventeen servo motors controlled by a computer. The motors are driven by wave intensity and frequency data from a National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration data buoy in the Pacific (station 51003, or station 46246 in the 2011 WRO version), so that visitors see the grid reproduce the movement of water at that distant location. A version driven by wave data recorded on Lake Superior was also made in 2011.

title: Templo da água: rio Tietê
summary: A circular sound installation in which long copper flutes connected to glass bulbs are suspended and moved by a mechanical system that dips them into a basin of water; the filling and emptying of the bulbs pushes air through the tubes and makes them sound. The water was collected from the upper Tietê River, is kept oxygenated during the show and was to be returned to the river afterwards. Visitors sit on benches arranged around the basin and listen; at the 36th Bienal de São Paulo the work was also activated by performances by Vásquez and Esmeralda Ramírez (Werebere group).

title: Terminus
summary: Terminus is a virtual reality work in five parts built from drawings by Jess Johnson, animated by Simon Ward with developer Kenny Smith and soundtracks by Andrew Clarke. Commissioned by the National Gallery of Australia and The Balnaves Foundation, it opened at the NGA in May 2018, where each part was housed in its own architectural structure on a full-scale tessellated floor map. Wearing a headset, the visitor passes through five realms (Fleshold Crossing, Known Unknown, Scumm Engine, Gog & Magog, Tumblewych), selecting each by looking at a portal, with no hand controllers.

title: The 3rd I
summary: The 3rd I (3rdi) is a camera surgically mounted on the back of Wafaa Bilal's head that, from 15 December 2010 and for a planned year, took an image automatically once a minute and sent it via a laptop carried on his body and a 3G connection to the website 3rdi.me. Commissioned by Mathaf: Arab Museum of Modern Art, Doha, for the exhibition Told/Untold/Retold, it was also shown there as a three-room installation in which banks of screens display the images and respond to the number and movement of visitors.

title: The Maw Of
summary: A web-based animation with an augmented-reality layer, commissioned for the Whitney Museum's artport and co-commissioned by KW Institute for Contemporary Art, Berlin. In the browser, a ghostly female figure drawn in a manga style moves through layers of interfaces, elements of whitney.org, a graph of the nervous system, a web console, parental-guidance alerts and military infrared imagery; scanning an on-screen QR code opens an AR layer on the viewer's phone that adds text and moves the figure out of the browser onto the device. title: The Refusal of Time
summary: The Refusal of Time is a half-hour, five-channel video installation made for dOCUMENTA (13) in Kassel in 2012, developed from conversations between Kentridge and historian of science Peter Galison about the history of the control of time. title: Toposcan / Baden-Württemberg
summary: A computer-based video installation on eight horizontally aligned 16:9 flat screens driven by eight Mac mini computers, with two loudspeakers. title: Transits

title: Unknown Label
summary: Unknown Label is a single- or multi-channel video installation of about 16 minutes about online micro-workers in Venezuela, Kenya and the Philippines who outline and label images ("image segmentation") used to train self-driving cars for German and US car manufacturers. It was developed in 2023 during a European Media Art Platform residency at Werkleitz, received an Honorary Mention in New Animation Art at Prix Ars Electronica 2024, and was later released for cinema as Their Eyes (2025, with Lucas Azémar).

title: VFRAME: Visual Forensics and Metadata Extraction
summary: VFRAME (Visual Forensics and Metadata Extraction) is a research project and open-source computer-vision toolkit by Adam Harvey for human rights researchers and investigative journalists who work with large archives of conflict-zone video. It began in 2017 as a prototype using object detection to locate illegal munitions in footage of the Syrian conflict, was developed with the Syrian Archive and Mnemonic.org into a visual search engine for million-scale video datasets, and from 2019 used 3D-modelled synthetic training images, for example of the AO-2.5RT cluster munition, to train detectors for objects with few real examples. It received an Award of Distinction in Artificial Intelligence & Life Art at the Prix Ars Electronica 2019.

title: Vigil

title: Voices of Aliveness
summary: Voices of Aliveness invites participants to ride bicycles equipped with a GPS recorder and a video camera along a 'shouting circuit' at La Martinière near Nantes, France, and to shout as loud as they can during the ride. summary: Wa akhiran musiba (At Last, a Tragedy) is a 15'49" video written, directed, shot and produced by Maya Shurbaji (editing Ayman Nahle, sound design Ziad Moukarzel). title: Walled Unwalled
summary: Walled Unwalled is a 20-minute single-channel video installation in which Lawrence Abu Hamdan, filmed behind the windows of recording booths in the Funkhaus studios in former East Berlin (the GDR state radio headquarters), delivers a monologue on legal cases in which evidence was heard or experienced through walls, doors or floors. title: Wantee
summary: Wantee is a film installation, commissioned by Tate and Grizedale Arts for the exhibition Schwitters in Britain at Tate Britain in 2013, in which a film tells a fictional story of Prouvost's grandfather, a conceptual artist and friend of Kurt Schwitters, who disappeared while digging a tunnel from his home towards Africa. title: Wellenwald mit Bunker
summary: Wellenwald mit Bunker is an installation of a spruce trunk covered in aluminium foil, leaning on a concrete object shaped like a bunker; antennae mounted on the trunk are wired into the concrete object. Inside, a speaker plays a composed drone sound file together with signals the antennae pick up from electromagnetic waves of nearby devices such as mobile phones, so visitors' devices alter the sound in real time. It is a reinterpretation of Joseph Beuys's 1972 work Fichtenstamm mit Munitionskiste (Munitionskiste mit Fichtenstamm).

title: With the Heart Coming Out of the Mouth (Com o coração saindo pela boca)
summary: With the Heart Coming Out of the Mouth was Brazil's presentation at the 59th Venice Biennale (2022), curated by Jacopo Crivelli Visconti. Built on an index of more than 200 Brazilian idiomatic expressions that name body parts, it combines sculptures, photographs and a video; visitors enter through an outsized ear and leave through another, and at intervals a large fabric heart drops from a mouth in the ceiling and inflates to fill the second room. The expressions are captioned in Portuguese, English and Italian.

title: Without Us
summary: Without Us is a project by composer and percussionist Daniel Brandt made up of an album (Erased Tapes, March 2025), a 20-minute short film of the same name directed with Anthony Dickenson and shot in Athens in 2023, and a live performance in which the concert is interwoven with the film. The film follows Gaia, an Uber driver who decides humanity is the world's problem; the album uses field recordings including the hum of Europe's largest mall. The live A/V version premiered at the Barbican in London in April 2025 and was presented at CTM Festival 2026.

title: Written To Not Remain
summary: Written To Not Remain is a 12'30" video work about writing on walls across post-revolution Libya since 2011. It combines archival imagery from a photo archive of over 200 images of wall writings that Barnosa began collecting in 2019 with acts made inside a VR simulation and 3D spatial scans, alongside a text recitation. It is listed among the S+T+ARTS Prize 2025 winners (Ars Electronica).

title: Zoom, Click, Waltz
summary: Zoom, Click, Waltz is a multimedia installation of 13 LED screens, each showing a person or people in a separate apartment window, dancing or not. It began during Singapore's 2020 Covid-19 'Circuit Breaker' lockdown, when the artist mailed letters to neighbours in her building asking them to dance by their living-room windows at a set time; the recordings are stitched together with staged, found and borrowed footage. It was shown at Gillman Barracks, Singapore (21 January - 7 February 2021) and won the 2021 Lumen Prize 3D/Interactive Award.

title: ÑUQA KAUSAKUSAQ QHEPAYKITAPAS / I WILL OUTLIVE YOU
summary: A single-channel HD video with sound (about 15 minutes) using 3-D animation, made after the artist encountered a 1200-year-old Moche ceramic vessel at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin depicting a prisoner about to be sacrificed. In a monologue, the prisoner reflects on the time before his death, his childhood, his transformation into a digital being and his incarceration as an object on museum display and part of an artwork. It was shown in Martínez Garay's solo exhibition I WILL OUTLIVE YOU at GRIMM, New York (2018) and at the 21st Bienal Sesc_Videobrasil (2019).
